relevance_note: Case report of a homozygous LCAT variant carrier with familial LCAT deficiency: 'Direct sequencing showed that this patient was homozygous for a novel mutation in exon 5 of the LCAT gene'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON and cut table-row spans from Table 1 (patients as columns; column header row 'ID' with Ⅱ-1, Ⅱ-2 (proband), Ⅱ-4, Ⅲ-2), checked against the table. Proband labelled with the paper's pedigree ID Ⅱ-2 from Table 1 (text calls her 'the patient'). Three relatives from Table 1 (Ⅱ-1, Ⅱ-4, Ⅲ-2) are included as family members described in relation to the proband; their relationship to her is not stated in text (pedigree figure only), they were not genotyped ('we have not measured LCAT activity or genotyped for the mutation in these family members'), so they have no variant rows. Their data were 'adopted from the results of regular health checks'. Contradiction: Results text lists the family members as 'Ⅱ-1, Ⅱ-4 and Ⅲ-1' whereas Table 1 has Ⅲ-2; Ⅲ-2's low HDL is taken from the Discussion's 'Three of the family members' (Table 1) as a group statement. The Table 1 urine protein '-' cells are not defined in a legend, so proteinuria is not reported for the relatives. Table 1 'Age' has no unit; ISO durations assume years. Age at diagnosis left not reported: the paper gives diagnosis of hypocholesterolemia '8 years ago' but no age at diagnosis of LCAT deficiency. Hypertriglyceridemia excluded for the proband from 'relatively low plasma level of triglyceride'. CKD/renal failure excluded from 'normal renal function' and normal renal function tests despite mild proteinuria. 'No history or signs of coronary heart disease' is narrower than the checklist item atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, so that item is not reported. protein_hgvs_as_stated holds 'G179R' (no p. notation printed). The Fig.2 legend repeats the variant text; spans come from the main text.

span: She also had hypothyroidism, which had been treated with levothyroxin for 2 years.
The progression of nephropathy may have been delayed in this patient because she was a vegetarian.

disease_label_as_stated.span: is supportive of the diagnosis of classical LCAT deficiency

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: both: deficient plasma LCAT activity with corneal opacity, mild hemolytic anemia and very low HDL-C, plus direct sequencing showing a homozygous LCAT mutation
span: In this case, the deficiency of plasma LCAT activity, which was associated with corneal opacity, mild hemolytic anemia and a very low HDL-C level, is supportive of the diagnosis of classical LCAT deficiency.
Direct sequencing showed that this patient was homozygous for a novel mutation in exon 5 of the LCAT gene (Fig.2).

functional_evidence_statement.value: In HEK293 cells the G179R mutant protein was present in the cell lysate but not detected in the medium (defective secretion), and LCAT activity was barely detectable in lysate or medium; patient plasma LCAT activity <50 nmol/mL/hr (almost undetectable)
span: In vitro expression of recombinant LCAT proteins in HEK293 cells showed that the mutant G179R protein was present in the cell lysate, but not the culture medium.
LCAT activity was barely detectable in the cell lysate or medium of the cells expressing the G179R mutant.
the mutant LCAT (LCAT G179R) was not detected in the medium (Fig.3A)
LCAT activity (＜50 nmol/mL/hr) was almost undetectable.

span: This novel missense mutation seems to cause a complete loss of catalytic activity of LCAT
we believe that the homozygous mutation G179R in LCAT accounts for the clinical manifestations in this case of FLD
